'''David George Hitlin''' (born 15 April 1942) is a professor at the [[California Institute of Technology]],<ref name="Caltech" /> specializing in experimental particle physics.

He was educated at [[Columbia University]], where he received his B.A. in 1963, and Ph.D. in 1968.<ref name="Caltech">{{cite web | title=David G. Hitlin | website=Caltech Division of Physics, Mathematics and Astronomy | url=http://pma.caltech.edu/people/david-g-hitlin | access-date=7 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Reunion and Dean's Day 2013 {{!}} Columbia College Today |url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct/archive/summer13/webexclusive/reunion_and_dean_s_day_2013 |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=www.college.columbia.edu}}</ref>

In 1986 he was elected a [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] ''for contributions to the study of weak decays of K mesons, particularly measurements of CP violating parameters and form factors, and for measurements of hadronic states produced in the decay of the psi meson and detailed studies of the weak decays of charmed particles"''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1986&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows archives|publisher=APS|accessdate=22 September 2020}}</ref> In 2016 he was awarded their [[Panofsky Prize]] ''"for leadership in the BABAR and Belle experiments, which established the violation of CP symmetry in B meson decay, and furthered our understanding of quark mixing and quantum chromodynamics."''<ref name="Panofsky">{{cite web | title=2016 W.K.H. Panofsky Prize in Experimental Particle Physics Recipient| website=American Physical Society| url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Hitlin&first_nm=David&year=2016| access-date=7 October 2018}}</ref> His co-awardees were Drs. [[Jonathan M. Dorfan|Jonathan Dorfan]], Fumihiko Takasaki, and Stephen L. Olsen.
